output.brief: FCR fell because of the 14 April Finance change, not the new starters. It cut the credit agents can apply on a call from £100 to £25, and larger adjustments now go automatically to the Billing Resolution team. Billing calls referred there jumped from 7% to 54% that week. Referred calls resolve at about 33% and non-referred at 82%, and both rates are unchanged. The mix shift explains the drop. The April intake refers at the same rate as veterans (56% vs 53–54%), and tenured agents' FCR fell by the same amount, so intake inexperience is not the cause. Tariff-enquiry FCR held at 85%, and the dashboard fell before the IVR change on 28 April. Customer Operations was not consulted on the change and no training was given. I am fairly confident. Next steps: don't put the April intake on performance plans, and don't pause the IVR work. Agree a revised credit limit with Finance, with post-call sampling. Trial it on two teams for six weeks, tracking FCR and unsupported credits, as the financial controller has said she would accept. Then decide on wider rollout. Ask MI for a team-level breakdown, which takes a day, rather than a three-month dashboard rebuild.
